name: finch-image-gen
description: Generate and edit images with OpenAI GPT Image 2.5 (or an OpenAI-compatible relay): text-to-image, image-to-image, masked edits, transparent backgrounds and custom sizes, right inside Finch.

scripts.build: node tools/build-icons.mjs && esbuild src/index.ts --bundle --platform=node --format=esm --target=node20 --outfile=dist/index.js && esbuild src/gallery.ts --bundle --platform=browser --target=chrome120 --outfile=dist/gallery.js && cp src/gallery.html src/gallery.css dist/
scripts.prepublishOnly: npm run typecheck && npm run build && npx @finchtoys/minitools doctor .

finch.name: Image 2.5
finch.description: Generate and edit images with OpenAI GPT Image 2.5 (or an OpenAI-compatible relay), with a masonry gallery you can re-edit from: text-to-image, image-to-image, masked edits, transparent backgrounds and custom sizes.
finch.systemPrompt: Use image_gen_create to generate images with OpenAI's image API. Text-to-image: pass only prompt. Image-to-image / reference-guided editing: also pass reference_image_paths (local absolute file paths); add mask_path to limit the edit to a masked area. COST POLICY: unless the user explicitly asks for something better, keep the cheap defaults — model gpt-image-2.5-flare, quality low, size 1024x1024. Do not upgrade quality or resolution on your own initiative; quality goes low → medium → high → xhigh → max and both quality and size drive cost and waiting time. Only switch to gpt-image-2.5-sunburst when precise editing matters, and say why when you do. size takes 'auto' or WIDTHxHEIGHT (1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536, 2048x2048, 2560x1440, 3840x2160 …). Set background='transparent' (with png or webp) when the user needs a cut-out. For a long, high-quality single render, pass partial_images 1-3 so progress stays visible. Generated images are saved locally as absolute file paths in the tool result and are also collected in the Image 2.5 gallery (left sidebar App View, or the Image 2.5 panel inside a session) — tell the user that when they ask where their pictures went; do not re-download or re-encode them, and use wechat_send or Session attach to show or share them. Gallery edits attach a marked preview with red freehand strokes, numbered pins and all user comments. Use the ORIGINAL image path included in the annotation as reference_image_paths, not the marked evidence preview. Follow every comment; do not reproduce the red markup or numbered pins in the generated result. The user may instead have pulled the same instructions into the message text with the Image 2.5 toolbar button — when the message itself carries the edit request, follow that text and treat the attached image as the thing to change. When the edit was made from the sidebar App View — which has no input box — it arrives as a chat message with two images instead: the first is the ORIGINAL to edit and the second is the marked preview, and the message text lists each comment with its percentage position and the original file path to pass in reference_image_paths. If the tool reports the OpenAI API key is missing, tell the user to open the Image 2.5 entry in Toolcase, click its settings (gear) menu and choose "OpenAI API Key" to paste it in. That settings menu also holds the "API Base URL" for a proxy/relay endpoint instead of api.openai.com. The Image 2.5 button in the Composer toolbar sets the everyday generation defaults instead: default model, default quality and default size (a single image_gen_create call can still override model/quality/size, or base_url for a one-off endpoint). When a request is blocked or rejected, the tool returns the API error code and a remediation hint — follow the hint instead of retrying the identical request.
